articleTitle: Optical second-harmonic generation in isocyclic and heterocyclic organic compounds
abstract: Second-harmonic generation experiments show that large optical nonlinearities are associated with isocyclic and heterocyclic organic groups. The nonlinearities in one compound of the pyrimidine family, 5-Nitrouracil, are estimated to be as large as in barium-sodium niobate.

articleTitle: Rapid photobleaching of organic laser dyes in continuously operated devices
abstract: Rapid bleaching of Rhodamine 6G and several other dyes has been observed in capillary-guide liquid lasers longitudinally pumped at<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\lambda = 5145</tex>Å. This bleaching appears to be permanent and is shown to present a severe limitation to the operation of nonflowing continuously excited dye lasers. The rate of bleaching has been measured under a variety of conditions and is found to vary linearly with pump power, independent of geometry.

articleTitle: Nonlinear properties of cuprous halides
abstract: A study of the nonlinear properties of cuprous halides in the near infrared (YAG Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>laser) and in the medium infrared (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser) is presented. The second-order susceptibilities have been compared to those of quartz and GaAs. Coherence lengths were measured at 1.06 μ and for the four principal transition lines of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser. In addition some linear parameters such as refractive indices in the visible and absorption coefficients from 0.3 to 25 μ were determined. The large values of Miller's δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>of those compounds are consistent with Levine's bond-charge model.

articleTitle: Instabilities in the doubly resonant parametric oscillator: A theoretical analysis
abstract: This paper is a theoretical examination of the frequency instabilities of the doubly resonant parametric oscillator. Such instabilities, caused by attempts to resonate simultaneously fields of two frequencies in unstabilized dispersive optical cavities, largely account for the poor performance of early parametric oscillators. The effects of reducing the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>of one of the resonant cavities of the doubly resonant oscillator are treated in detail. An analysis is given that predicts the frequency instabilities resulting from the presence of a slight feedback at the nonresonant mode in a nearly singly resonant oscillator. The analysis shows that the nonresonant mode feedback must be completely eliminated to prevent double-cavity oscillator-frequency instabilities.

articleTitle: On the use of optical waveguide techniques for internal reflection spectroscopy
abstract: A detailed analysis is presented of the absorption of energy from a thin-film dielectric waveguide by an absorbing medium that is brought into contact with one wall of the dielectric guide. It is shown that the exponential decay constant for the mode of the guide so obtained can closely approach that obtained for the free wave in the absorbing medium alone. The dependence of the attenuation on the guide parameters is examined and means for overcoming some of the problems imposed by the guidance process are discussed. It is concluded that the techniques can offer greatly enhanced sensitivity over the conventional internal-reflection spectroscopy and yet retain the attractive features of small sample volume and easy sample preparation. The technique also offers the possibility of constructing microscopic probes for the examination of spectra in otherwise inaccessible places.

articleTitle: Output power calculations for a continuously pumped Q-switched YAG:Nd+3laser
abstract: A computational approach has been formulated to predict the average pulsed power output of a continuously pumped<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-switched YAG:Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+3</sup>laser. Using this technique the dependence of laser operational characteristics on parametric changes can be readily evaluated:<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-switch mechanization, optimized output coupling reflectance, effects of intracavity losses, and pumping efficiency on average pulsed power are some of the more important items. This theory was checked experimentally using a 10-30-W multimode and 1.4-W TEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</inf>mode laser operating at PRFs between 1 and 40 kHz; excellent correlation has been obtained.

articleTitle: Spatial hole-burning effects in a Nd3+:YAG laser
abstract: The concept of spatial hole burning in the population inversion distribution of a solid-state laser was introduced by Tang et al in 1963 [3]. In this paper, several aspects of the spatial hole-burning effect in a CW Nd:YAG laser are discussed, both theoretically and experimentally. The number of oscillating modes, transverse mode degeneracy, and effects of sinusoidal phase perturbations are included. The measured number of oscillating modes is in good agreement with the theory based on the treatments of Tang et al. The transverse mode degeneracy causes an output power dip by quenching higher order modes through the spatial hole-burning effect. The positions of dips are calculated taking into account the thermal focusing effect in a pumped YAG rod. Effects of phase perturbations are discussed using nonlinear rate equations, and it is shown that two kinds of resonances peculiar to the Nd:YAG laser can be excited by a subharmonic sinusoidal drive.

articleTitle: Influences of self-induced thermal effects on phase matching in nonlinear optical crystals
abstract: In nonlinear optical crystals useful for second-harmonic generation, index inhomogeneities introduced by the self-induced temperature profile due to the laser beam influence the phase-matching conditions for nonlinear optical interaction. We have found that broadening of the width of the central peak, increase of asymmetry, shift of the maximum towards higher temperature, disappearance of the subsidiary structure in the second-harmonic power versus temperature, and the reduction of the conversion efficiency for second-harmonic generation may be caused. These effects depend upon the total absorbed power in the crystal, the birefringence variations due to temperature, the thermal conductivity, and the wavelength.

articleTitle: Oscillation of the 1.833-µ line in Nd3+:YAG
abstract: This correspondence reports oscillation of the<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F_{32} \rightarrow</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I_{15/2}, 1.833-\mu</tex>transition in Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:YAG. Peak<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-switched output powers of 10 kW at 50 pps have been obtained.

articleTitle: Ultrahigh-speed photography of picosecond light pulses
abstract: A new technique for the display of picosecond light pulses is presented. Ultrashort (6 ps) green light pulses passing through a light-scattering medium are photographed from the side by a camera positioned behind a shutter of 10-ps framing time. The shutter is an ultrafast Kerr cell driven by infrared pulses 8 ps in duration. Color photographs show a bright spot on a dark background, revealing the unambiguous presence of well-isolated picosecond light pulses. The shape of the spot is the result of a convolution involving the three-dimensional shape of the green pulse and the time transmission function of the shutter, this function being dictated by the shape of the infrared pulse. The experiment indicates that a new technique for visualizing light pulses consists in simply observing their flight through a scattering medium from behind an ultrafast shutter having a framing time equal to the time resolution desired. The new technique has many advantages over the two-photon fluorescence display technique, such as higher sensitivity, wider spectral range, and easier interpretation. The ultrafast camera also can be used for the photographic measurement of ultrashort relaxation times in dielectrics and in fluorescent dyes.

articleTitle: TEM00enhancement in CW Nd-YAG by thermal lensing compensation
abstract: A technique for the calculation of a thermal-lens aberration compensation in a CW Nd-YAG laser is presented. The results of an empirical verification are also given. An increase from 2 to 25 W in 1.06 μm TEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</inf>power output was obtained after the crystal was compensated.

articleTitle: Influence of self-induced thermal effects on second-harmonic generation
abstract: In optical nonlinear crystals used for second-harmonic generation the presence of absorption at the fundamental wavelength can lead to index of refraction inhomogeneities that reduce the conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: Power and efficiency of a continuous HF chemical laser
abstract: Experimental measurements of laser power output and chemical efficiency are reported for a continuous HF chemical laser. In this device, arc-heated N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>is mixed in a plenum with SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>to provide F atoms. The mixture is expanded to form a supersonic jet into which H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>is diffused. Population inversion and lasing are due to H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>+ F → HF(υ) + H,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon \leq 3, \Delta</tex>H = -31.7 kcal. Power levels up to 1 kW have been obtained. The efficiency of conversion of chemical energy to laser power is 16 percent at low SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>flow rates and approximately 10 percent at peak power. For a fixed arc power, addition of O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>into the plenum raises peak power by about 25 percent under present operating conditions and reduces sulphur deposition on mirror surfaces. The presence of HF and DF in the plenums of DF and HF lasers, respectively, did not appear to degrade laser performance. (HF and DF levels up to 10 percent of the local F concentration were studied.) However, the presence of HF and DF in the plenums of HF and DF lasers, respectively, did degrade laser output. For given flow conditions, peak net laser power was obtained when the optical cavity axis was about 2 cm downstream of the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>injection station. The net output power was reduced to zero when the cavity axis location was increased to 5 cm.

articleTitle: Acoustooptical deflections in thin films
Thermal transient effects in optically pumped repetitively pulsed lasers
abstract: An approximate formulation of the thermal transient effects in laser rods, such as the temperature distribution in the laser rod and the effect of rod distortion on a collimated light beam passing through the rod, is described. Also, a computation is made for a practical case and compared to experimental results.

articleTitle: Crystal symmetry effects on nonlinear optical processes in optical waveguides
abstract: A general three-wave nonlinear (NL) optical interaction can be phase matched using the dispersion of optical waveguide modes. The phase-match condition can be fine tuned by varying the direction of propagation in a two-dimensional waveguide and using a birefringent NL material with an orientation that preserves TE and TM mode propagation. Two general cases are found where this technique is possible. The effects of crystal symmetry and orientation on the size of the NL interaction are calculated for all birefringent crystal classes and cubic crystal classes.

articleTitle: Selective two-step (STS) photoionization of atoms and photodissociation of molecules by laser radiation
Laser action of dyes in gelatin
abstract: High-gain directional stimulated emission has been observed for a number of dyes in gelatin with pumping by a nitrogen laser or a liquid dye laser. For some dyes the gel is made with water and gelatin; for others a detergent must be added or glycerin used instead of water.

articleTitle: Laser glass composition and the possibility of eliminating electrostrictive effects
abstract: Many authors have stated that electrostrictive self-trapping of the light beam initiates laser damage in solid transparent dielectrics. By systematically varying composition, it may be possible to find a glass in which electrostrictive effects are eliminated.

articleTitle: Improved electrooptic materials for holographic storage applications
Performance of an unstable oscillator on a 30-kW CW gas dynamic laser
abstract: Mode-control experiments at a 30-kW CW power level with an unstable resonator at a high Fresnel number were performed on a gas dynamic laser. Near- and far-field intensity distributions were obtained that are consistent with theoretical values for an approximately twice diffraction-limited beam. Under these conditions, the output power was more than half of the maximum multi-mode power.

articleTitle: Excitation of an atmospheric-pressure CO2-N2-He laser by capacitor discharges
abstract: The design of a new type of atmospheric pressure CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-He laser capable of producing 1.2-J infrared light pulses with a peak power of 0.5 MW is described. An investigation of the laser output dependence on gas flow, gas mixture, capacitor voltage, output coupling reflectivity, and electrode spacing was made. It is shown that even greater energies and powers should be possible at higher voltages and larger electrode gaps.

articleTitle: GaAs-laser-induced population inversion in the ground-state hyperfine levels of Cs133
abstract: This paper describes the achievement of population inversion among the hyperfine levels in the ground state of Cs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">133</sup>by optically pumping these atoms with radiation from a GaAs diode laser. The laser output was used to monitor the populations in the two ground-state hyperfine levels as well as to perform the hyperfine pumping. By varying the injection current, a GaAs laser operated CW at about 77°K was used to scan the 8521-Å line of Cs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">133</sup>. The intensity of the resonance scattering from cesium vapor served as an indicator of the populations of the two levels involved. Experiments were performed both with neon-filled and with paraflint-coated cells containing the cesium vapor. It was discovered that the diode laser could easily be tuned by manually adjusting the injection current to match either of the hyperfine components of the D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>optical transition. Possible future applications, including a restudy of the light shifts, the construction of a cesium maser, and the physics of optical pumping with coherent light are discussed.

articleTitle: Excitation and relaxation in a high-pressure CO laser
abstract: Strong laser emission is reported from a transverse discharge at relatively high pressure in both pure CO and CO-He at room temperature. Calculations of excited population distributions produced by electron CO collisions show an initial distribution that is approximately Boltzmann at a vibrational temperature<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T_{\upsilon}\simeq 6700</tex>K. The laser emission spectra exhibit complete inversion. Time delay measurements are in good agreement with known V-V relaxation times in CO, and the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p\tau</tex>product shows the constancy expected of vibrational relaxation. The evolution of inversion from a near Boltzmann distribution can only be explained by anharmonic oscillator relaxation effects.

articleTitle: Investigation of tellurium for frequency doubling with CO2lasers
abstract: Second-harmonic generation (SHG) of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser radiation with tellurium has been investigated. The nonlinear coefficient was measured (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d_{11} =1.6 \times 10^{-6}</tex>ESU), as were the peak and average power damage thresholds (2-4 MW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>and 150 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). Finally, the SHG conversion efficiency was found to saturate due to increased absorption of the fundamental.

articleTitle: Signal structure of continuously self-pulsing GaAs lasers
abstract: CW-excited GaAs lasers can emit self-induced pulses. To study these pulses we have used an intensity correlator involving phase-matched second-harmonic generation in LiIO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Besides measuring the pulsewidth and the repetition rate we investigated the amplitude fluctuations within a pulse and the correlation between fluctuations of consecutive pulses.

articleTitle: On the spiking phenomenon in organic dye lasers
abstract: The spiking condition of dye lasers is analyzed by means of a small-signal approximation of the rate equations. Dye lasers are generally operated close to the border region between spiking and nonspiking. An initial spike is observed in the output beam of a flash-lamp-excited rhodamine 6G laser with a shortened cavity.

articleTitle: Pulsed discharge initiated chemical lasers - Part II: HF laser emission from NF3and N2F4systems
abstract: A transverse, multiple-arc pulsed discharge has produced laser emission in NF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>mixed with H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, HCl, HBr, and natural gas.<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P_{10}, P_{21}, P_{32}</tex>, and P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">43</inf>HF transitions were observed. The peak powers measured ranged from ∼8.5 to 25 kW with typical pulsewidths of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\sim0.3 \mu</tex>s.

articleTitle: Oblique-cut longitudinal electrooptic modulators
abstract: The minimum longitudinal half-wave voltages are calculated for five oxygen-octahedral crystals with large linear electrooptic coefficients. The predicted values range from 11 kV (LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) to 75 V (BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>). Experimental results have been obtained for LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>and LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. The minima occur in directions with finite birefringence; the resulting limitations in angular aperture and temperture sensitivity are considered, and a compensation scheme to off-set them is discussed. The limiting operating frequency for uncompensated modulators can stem from joule heating in the transparent electrodes. The effect is evaluated and a figure of merit is derived. The values are surprisingly similar for the five crystals considered.

articleTitle: Laser-controlled switching
abstract: A new type of laser switching is discussed. The laser produces volume ionization in the path of a propagating streamer, increasing its velocity. Subnanosecond jitter is thereby obtained with pressurized gas switches.

articleTitle: Transition selection with adjustable outcoupling for a laser device applied to CO2
abstract: In this paper we discuss the possibilities and realization in high-power systems of a narrow-band reflector with adjustable high reflectivity and with continuous tuning over a large frequency region. We describe a design for both low- and high-gain systems. For the experimental realization of a low-gain system we used a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser and studied a continuous range of 65 transitions of the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00\deg1-02\deg0</tex>and 13 transitions of the 01<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>1-11<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>0 vibrational band. With a cavity containing a dc discharge 130 cm long, for each band we found a continuous range of single oscillating transitions with output powers up to 15 W. Finally, we propose an experimental solution for continuous tuning of a high-gain system as, for instance, the central part of the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00\deg1-10\deg0</tex>vibrational band of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Analysis of giant pulse amplification in Nd3+doped glass
abstract: In a study of the mechanism of giant pulse amplification in Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>doped glass, the following measurements have been made: 1) energy extracted from an amplifier as a function of the input energy, 2) relative fluorescence intensity at 0.9μ in a slab, pumped by the emission of a ruby laser, and 3) gain variation after the transit of an intense, short, rectangular pulse. The experimental results have been compared to theoretical results from a model where both metastable and terminal levels are regarded as comprising two components. The unknown multiplicity of the lower component of the terminal level g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>appears as a parameter. It is assumed that during the pulse duration, Boltzmann distribution is maintained between the components of each level. A finite terminal level lifetime τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>may be introduced in the model. Best agreement is obtained with the following values of the parameters: amplification cross section<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\sigma_{21}\simeq 1.8.10^{-20}</tex>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g_{11} = 1</tex>or 2, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\tau_{11} \geq 100</tex>ns.

articleTitle: Long-pulse dye-laser emission across the visible spectrum
abstract: Long-pulse laser emission has been obtained across the visible spectrum using six different organic dyes in solution with triplet-state quenching additives, suggesting many new candidates for CW dye-laser operation.

articleTitle: Performance of a transversely excited pulsed HF laser
abstract: Operation of a pulsed HF laser with unique spectral and temporal behavior is reported.<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</tex>-branch oscillation in the 1-0 band and peak multiline powers of 700 kW in 200-ns pulses have been observed. The gain of the 75-cm laser was measured to be 235 dB.

articleTitle: Continuous visible and near-infrared laser action in Hg II
abstract: CW laser oscillation from singly ionized mercury at 6150 and 7945 Å has been observed in a transverse-discharge slotted hollow-cathode laser. Population inversion is attributed to charge transfer and Penning-type ionization reactions.

articleTitle: Parasitic noise on the output of a CW YAG:Nd+3laser
abstract: An experimental investigation was conducted to reduce the parasitic noise appearing on the output of a 6-W CW YAG:Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+3</sup>laser. Initially, low-frequency fluctuations as high as 30 percent and relaxation oscillation bursts exceeding 80 percent of the CW power level were present. Low-frequency modulation was reduced by the addition of an active feedback loop to control lamp current. Relaxation oscillations were determined to be influenced by laser rod cooling, pump-lamp aging, vibration, and intracavity optical interface quality. At the conclusion of the program, low-power fluctuations and relaxation oscillation excursions did not exceed 2 percent.

articleTitle: Enhanced optical third-harmonic generation by coupled nonlinear absorption
abstract: Combined nonlinear absorption and third-harmonic generation has resulted in enhanced harmonic output in a liquid-dye medium phase matched by anomalous dispersion. The measured absorption is employed in calculating the third-harmonic power.

articleTitle: On the excitation mechanism of the He-Zn laser
abstract: By means of fluorescence, decay measurements in a He-Zn pulsed afterglow, the Zn II laser transitions at 5894 and 7479 Å have been assigned to Penning collisions with He(2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>) metastable atoms. The Zn II 6102-Å transition is ascribed to charge transfer collisions with He+. Penning and charge transfer cross sections are presented.

articleTitle: Infrared pulse transmission in SF6-He mixtures
abstract: The transmission of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-switched CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser pulses through SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-He mixtures is studied experimentally and compared with predictions generated by computer calculations based on a four-state model for SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>. The results show that for saturating fields the factor determining the rate of absorption is the rotational energy transfer process that feeds the levels interacting with the laser. This conclusion has implications for models of passive<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>switching in molecular lasers and infrared-infrared double resonance.

articleTitle: Excited-state absorption of SF6at 936.8 cm-1
abstract: An effect that is opposite to saturable absorption in the infrared was observed when a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser beam was passed through SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>. An increase of absorption occurred when the radiant flux of the laser was increased to 10 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The effect was observed for the P(28) line of the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00\deg1-10\deg0</tex>band of the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser, and was attributed to absorption from excited vibrational states of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>.

articleTitle: Higher order intensity correlations of optical pulses
abstract: A simple statistical model of a noisy optical pulse is used to derive concise analytic expressions for the contrast ratios of nonlinear pulsewidth measurements. The results are sufficiently general to be used as an aid in the interpretation of intensity correlation experiments using either<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</tex>th-order multiphoton absorption or<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</tex>th-order harmonic generation. The amplitude of the spike is expected to be much larger in the higher order experiments.

articleTitle: Effect of inductance on the small-signal gain of a transverse-excitation atmospheric-pressure discharge in carbon dioxide
abstract: An external inductance was placed in the circuit of a resistive transverse-excitation atmospheric discharge to observe its effect on the small-signal gain of a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-He-N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>gas mix. The results of the measurements indicate that by lowering the inductance of the circuit, less helium is required in the gas in order to obtain a uniform discharge; consequently, more CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>may be used with higher gains resulting.

articleTitle: Ho3+laser action in YAlO3at 2.119 µ
abstract: Pulsed laser action at 2.119 μ has been observed from Ho<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>in a crystal of YAlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>sensitized with Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>and Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>. A linearly polarized output of 1.2 J was obtained at 77°K. Measurements of the anisotropy of the stimulated-emission cross sections are reported.

articleTitle: Parameter studies of pulsed HF lasers
abstract: The average output power of pulsed HF chemical lasers is found to depend strongly on the fluorine source used. The best performance was obtained from H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-He mixes, which gave average powers of 850 mW and energies of 20 mJ/pulse. Peak gains of at least 0.036 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>are observed. Average powers of 450 mW from DF and 70 mW from HCl are reported.

articleTitle: Widening of spectral lines in an Ar+laser
abstract: In this paper an investigation of the spectral line widths and shifts of Ar I and Ar II lines in argon ion laser plasma is carried out. The discharge-tube internal diameters were 5 and 7 mm, the current densities were 113, 163, and 242 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the pressures were 0.68, 0.42, and 0.23 torr. Approximate calculations were made of ion and electron temperatures, electron density, ion mean free path, and charge-exchange cross section. It was determined that ion-neutral charge-exchange collisions play an important role in this type of plasma.

articleTitle: A CO2-laser-triggered spark gap
abstract: A coaxial spark gap triggered by a high-pressure CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser has been constructed. High-voltage pulses with subnanosecond rise time and very low jitter have been obtained. The observed low-laser energy threshold required to initiate switching suggests an application of the spark gap in controlling and manipulating high-intensity infrared radiation by electrooptic shutters.

articleTitle: CW laser oscillation at 5433 Å in neon
abstract: CW laser oscillation at 5433 Å has been observed in the He-Ne laser. The transition is from the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3S_{2}</tex>to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2p_{10}</tex>level and is the 9th in this group of nine allowed transitions to exhibit laser oscillation.

articleTitle: Thermal effects of a continuously pumped Nd3+:YAG laser
abstract: Thermal effects in a Nd:YAG laser rod, which is pumped continuously by tungsten iodine lamps, are described. Measurements using a 0.6328-μman probe beam yielded temperature distribution in and at the boundary of the rod. The results of birefringence and focal length are consistent with theoretical treatments, if an effective heat conversion coefficient peculiar to the apparatus is assumed. The resonance condition of an optical resonator containing a rod exhibiting focusing effect is discussed.

articleTitle: High-pressure transverse-discharge CO laser
abstract: Experiments with a high-pressure transverse-discharge CO laser are described. The pulsed laser output was observed to occur on several CO rotational-vibrational transitions in bands from<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon = 6 \rightarrow \upsilon = 5</tex>to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon = 11 \rightarrow \upsilon = 10</tex>. A study of the laser delay time versus CO pressure is presented and its relation to two inversion schemes is discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Signature variations with mirror separation for small sealed CO2lasers
abstract: A detailed experimental study of laser signature as a function of laser mirror distance variations is reported. This was done for small sealed low-power CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>lasers (≈ 1 watt) of the type useful in laser communication. It is shown that most laser-output profiles change drastically from half-wavelength to half-wavelength except the strong P(20) line, which seems to remain relatively constant. Frequency width is given for many of the laser output profiles appearing in the various signatures observed. Line competition is also discussed.

articleTitle: New N2-pumped ultraviolet dye lasers
abstract: Laser action in BBD and isopropyl-PBD pumped by the N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser has been observed. The energy outputs, optimum concentrations, and wavelength ranges for several ultraviolet-lasing dyes were also determined.

articleTitle: Forced and self-mode-locking of the krypton ion laser
abstract: Mode-locking of a krypton ion laser has been studied using a graphite-bore plasma tube and acoustooptic modulator In forced mode locking, 0.2-ns pulses were achieved with the principal laser lines. In contrast with the argon laser, there is a marked tendency for self-locking in krypton.

articleTitle: Electron energy distribution in CO2laser discharges
abstract: Electrical plasma parameters of the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser were investigated by probe and high-frequency techniques. The electron energy distribution function was measured by the second derivative method. The relatively high-pressure effect on the electron probe current was taken into account when analyzing the experimental curves. The influence of the addition of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, He, Xe and the influence of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>dissociation on the plasma discharge properties were studied. Calculations of the pumping rates to vibrational levels taking part in creating inversion show that the influence on output power of a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser usually observed with the addition of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>and He cannot be explained by a changing of the electron component of the plasma. The increase of output power and efficiency with addition of Xe to the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser is connected with an essential changing of plasma parameters of the electron component.

articleTitle: A pin-electrode atmospheric-pressure CO2laser
abstract: A 1.2-m-long transversely excited atmospheric-pressure (TEA) CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser utilizing shower discharges is described and its operating characteristics as a function of voltage examined up to 60 kV. Pulse energies in excess of 2 J, peak powers in excess of 20 MW, and efficiencies up to 15 percent have been achieved.

articleTitle: Lutetium effects on the UV absorption spectra of Nd:YAG
abstract: Spectroscopic observations were made on Lu:Nd:YAG and Nd:YAG laser materials. Variations in the UV absorption strengths are described and related to the presence of Lu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>. These results indicate that an optimum Lu/Nd ion ratio exists that will yield minimum absorption by the host over the wavelength range<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4-0.24 \mu</tex>m. The reduction in absorption will minimize nonuniform heating effects that should lead to better laser performance under certain conditions.

articleTitle: Theory of an ultra-broad-band optical dielectric waveguide coupler system
abstract: A technique is described for operating a prism to dielectric thin-film waveguide system over a wide frequency band from a conventional broad-band source of the dye-laser type. The continuous coupling bandwidth can extend, typically, over a frequency range of twice to three times the center frequency. The experimental tolerances have been established and are shown to be within the capability of present-day technology.

articleTitle: High repetition rate TEA CO2laser
abstract: This correspondence reports on the successful operation of a TEA CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser at rates up to 1000 pps with an average output power up to 65 W over long periods of time. An essential feature of the present system is a rapid gas circulation transverse to the laser axis combined with a large volume of ambient gas. It is found that decomposition of the gas is one of the major problems at high repetition rates.

articleTitle: Self-focusing of 10.6-µm radiation in liquid CS2
abstract: Self-focusing of 9-kW CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser pulses was observed in liquid CS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The calculated coefficient of nonlinear index of refraction (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) from experimental data is approximately 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-17</sup>MKS, which is nearly three orders of magnitude larger than the nonlinear index coefficient observed for visible radiation.

articleTitle: Mass spectroscopic studies of the CO laser discharge
abstract: The effects of adding Xe, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>to the CO-He laser discharge are studied mass spectroscopically. Xe greatly reduces CO dissociation. H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>does not react chemically but alters discharge kinetics. O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>has little effect on the CO-Xe-He discharge but reduces CO dissociation in CO-He.

articleTitle: Efficient acoustooptic modulation at 3.39 and 10.6 µm in crystalline germanium
abstract: A Ge acoustooptic pulse modulator has been constructed and tested at 3.39 and 10.6 μm. A pulse rise time of 20 ns and deflection efficiency of 11 percent per watt of RF drive power when operating at 10.6 μm were realized.

articleTitle: Gas dynamic CO2-He-(N2) laser investigations
abstract: Experiments on IR laser action and gain measurements are reported for a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-containing gas mixture flow that cools as a result of expansion. The mixture is preheated by a reflected shock wave, and the gas is expanded into a vacuum through a slit. Laser action is obtained in a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-He mixture, while the addition of nitrogen increases the gain. The gain was found to depend on the distance from the slit and the gas pressure before the slit.

articleTitle: CO laser emission below 5.0 µ
abstract: Laser emission from a CW He-air-CO laser has been observed at 4.991, 4.937, 4.927, 4.884, and 4.874 μ. The emissions have been identified to result from transitions as low as<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon= 3 : 2</tex>.

articleTitle: Degradation of zinc-diffused GaAs electroluminescent diodes
abstract: A physical model is considered to describe the gradual degradation of Zn-diffused GaAs electroluminescent diodes. This model is based on the postulation that new recombination centers are formed during the degradation process. Evidence of the formation of these new centers is established through the measurement of the injected carrier lifetime. Experimental variations of quantum efficiencies, current-voltage characteristics, and light-current curves resulting from degradation tests are obtained. These experimental data agree with the calculated results based on the proposed model.

articleTitle: Continuous dye laser emission from 5220 to 6570 Å
Schaefer-Bergmann diffraction pattern due to the abnormal Bragg reflection in birefringent media
abstract: A new type of the Schaefer-Bergmann diffraction patterns originated from the abnormal Bragg reflection phenomenon in anisotropic media has been demonstrated using α quartz and monoclinic Pb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>crystals. The wave-vector direction of the diffracted light has been expressed in analytical equations for the general cases in uniaxial crystals as a function of those of the incident light beam and the acoustic wave, on the basis of the simple pseudo momentum conservation relation. The shape of the abnormal patterns can be determined using the equations and the known data on the acoustic and the optical wave-vector surfaces, and calculated patterns for α quartz are in good agreement with the observed ones. The equations predict that a small difference appears in the shape of the patterns between two cases where the polarization planes of the incident optical beams are orthogonal with each other, and this fact has been well confirmed by the present experiment.

articleTitle: Investigations of an unstable confocal resonator on a chemical laser system
abstract: Preliminary experimental results are reported on the successful mating of an unstable confocal resonator with an HF chemical laser.

articleTitle: Transverse mode locking using cylindrically symmetric modes
abstract: The possibility of transverse mode locking using cylindrically symmetric laser modes is considered. For a specified set of mode amplitudes and phases it is found that the beam intensity profile in the transverse plane is the same shape as the fundamental mode, but has a spot size that is time varying with the transverse-mode spacing frequency. The beam power is the sum of the powers of the individual modes.

articleTitle: High-efficiency driven Q switching of the CO2laser using the stark effect in molecular gases
abstract: High-efficiency driven<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>switching of the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser has been observed by the use of the Stark effect in CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Cl, CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F, CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>CHF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>= CF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Cl on various lines in both the 9.4- and 10.4-μ bands. The effect is observed with both pulsed and sinusoidal electric fields applied to the intracavity modulator.

articleTitle: Mode-locking of an atmospheric pressure cross-excited electrically pulsed CO2laser
abstract: Self-mode-locking of a cross-excited electrically pulsed CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser has been observed and studied as a function of cavity length and operating pressure. The best results are obtained at a pressure of 450 torr with cavity lengths on the order of 1m. Two-ns duration pulses have been measured, the shortest pulses observed to date at 10.6-μ wavelength. With longer cavities more axial modes are locked, resulting in a longer dead time between pulses; however, the pulsewidths increase with increasing cavity length. Mode-locking was not improved by the use of the bleachable absorber SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>.

articleTitle: On the possibility of phase-matched infrared mixing using induced birefringence
abstract: The possibility of inducing sufficient birefringence in acentric cubic crystals to permit the phase matching of nonlinear infrared mixing is examined. It is shown that the electrooptic effect is inadequate for this, while phase matching by uniaxial stress is unlikely but cannot be ruled out.

articleTitle: New unidentified high-gain oscillation at 486.1 and 434.0 nm in the presence of neon
abstract: High-gain oscillation at 486.1 and 434.0 nm has been observed in a pulsed neon laser that was simultaneously operating at 540.1 nm. The two previously unreported laser lines are tentatively identified as the Balmer β and γ lines of atomic hydrogen.

articleTitle: Mode competition and self-locking in a multipass CO2laser
abstract: Observation of self-locking is reported in a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>multipass laser. Phase-locked pulsing occurred at or in multiples of the cavity round-trip transit time. The observed pulse half-widths ranged from 60 to 70 ns.

articleTitle: Phase-matched upconversion of 10.6-µ radiation in ZnGeP2
Frequency doubling of 2.06-µm Ho-doped apatite laser output in Ag3AsS3
abstract: The 2.06-μm output of a holmium-doped silicon oxyapatite laser was successfully frequency doubled by means of a proustite single crystal. Frequency doubling to 1.03 μm permitted the use of an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S1</tex>photomultiplier for the accurate determination of the laser wavelength, linewidth, and temporal behavior. The experiment also demonstrated that intracavity second-harmonic generation provided better amplitude correlation between the fundamental and second harmonic than did extracavity generation.

articleTitle: CW measurements of the CO molecular laser
abstract: Gain measurements have been performed on 80 rotation-vibration<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</tex>-branch transitions of the CO laser. With these data, the gas temperature and the Einstein coefficient, the absolute population densities of the laser level have been calculated for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon= 7, 8, 9</tex>.

articleTitle: Small signal gain in the CO-air-He laser
abstract: The small-signal single-pass gain for 24 individual CO laser lines has been measured for a flowing CO-air-He laser. The vibrational-rotational<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P(J)_{\upsilon,\upsilon'}</tex>lines considered were for rotational transitions from<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">J = 10</tex>to 16 and upper vibrational levels from<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon = 7</tex>to 11. The maximum gain was observed for the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P(15)_{10,9}</tex>laser line, with an average logarithmic energy gain of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.633 \times 10^{-3}</tex>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: Pulsed N2O molecular laser studies
abstract: The afterglow pulse-gain technique was used to measure the relaxation of the 00°1 upper laser level in N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O from 300 to 700°K. The rate constant<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k_{N_{2}O}</tex>(torr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) varies with temperature as<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\log</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k_{N_{2}O} = 4.53 - 10.9T^{-1/3}</tex>. Measurements of the relaxation time at 300°K agree with the fluorescence technique results of Yardley [1]. Gain studies were also made with gas mixtures in a nonflowing system. Single-pulsed N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O + CO + He mixtures at 300°K showed considerable peak gain. However, subsequent pulses of these mixtures show that the gain is reduced because of the chemical reaction forming CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Measurements of this transformation from one molecular laser mixture to another are discussed.

articleTitle: Long-term frequency stabilization of a composite-cavity argon laser
abstract: A commercial argon laser was modified to radiate at a highly stable single frequency over a long time period. The long-term stability is obtained by controlling the mirror separation of the mode selector cavity, using the wavelength of a stabilized He-Ne laser as a reference. As a result the argon laser emits a maximum power of 450 mW at 4880 Å with a relative frequency stability<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\Delta\nu/\nu = 2.10^{-8}</tex>over one half-hour operation.

articleTitle: Doppler-effect mechanism for laser Q switching with a rotating mirror
abstract: A novel description, based on the Doppler effect, is given for laser<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>switching by a rotating mirror. Fourier analysis yields a relation between the width of the pulse<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\Deltat_{1/2}</tex>and the angular velocity of the mirror<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\dot{\theta}</tex>. It is shown that for laser emission having a Gaussian spatial amplitude profile the temporal shape of a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-switched pulse is also Gaussian. It is predicted that for different lasers<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>switched by mirrors rotating with the same<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\dot{\theta}, \Deltat_{1/2}</tex>will depend on the wavelength of the laser. For a ruby laser, measurements are reported of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\Deltat_{1/2}</tex>versus<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\dot{\theta}</tex>for different configurations of the cavity into which vertical and horizontal slits were introduced.

articleTitle: Comments on the identification of some xenon ion laser lines
abstract: Earlier measurements and level assignments made by the authors for some xenon ion laser lines are reevaluated in light of recent work by Gallardo and coworkers. The lines affected are the 5260.17-, 5260.43-, 4305.75-, and 3759.94-Å lines in xenon and 4647.40- and 4650.22-Å lines attributed to carbon.

articleTitle: 4.9-µ He-Air-CH4-(CO) laser
abstract: Low-vibrational-level<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P(J)_{\upsilon,\upsilon'}</tex>CO laser emissions have been measured from He-air-CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>mixtures. The CW lines below 5.0μ were measured in air to occur at 4.8836, 4.8935, 4.8974, 4.9072, 4.9366, 4.9466, 4.9670, and 4.9778μ. These emissions are tentatively identified to result from transitions as low as<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon = 3 : 2</tex>. Such emissions were relatively more frequent with CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>than with CO specifically.

articleTitle: Reduced modulator drive-power requirements for 10.6-µ guided waves
abstract: It is shown that a reduction of more than an order of magnitude in electrooptic modulator drive power requirements should be possible at 10.6 μ by the use of a dielectric slab waveguide, despite the dimensional limitations imposed by electrode absorption.

articleTitle: Proposed electrooptical PCM multiplexer-demultiplexer
abstract: A reciprocal time multiplexer-demultiplexer for optical PCM is proposed. The device is based on the coincidence of an optical pulse and a modulating voltage pulse in an electrooptic crystal. Both a lumped and a traveling-wave configuration are described.

articleTitle: Helium cleanup in the helium-cadmium laser discharge
abstract: We have observed a rapid loss of helium from the discharge volume when operating certain types of sealed-off helium-cadmium laser tubes. In severe cases, a loss over a hundred times larger than that possible by diffusion through the glass walls has been observed. Experiments are described indicating that the lost helium is trapped in cadmium, which condenses on the tube walls in the vicinity of the active discharge. Possible trapping mechanisms are discussed. An improved discharge tube design is presented that effectively eliminates the helium cleanup.

articleTitle: CO(v = 2:1) laser transitions from He-air-CH4
abstract: A flowing electrochemically excited liquid-nitrogen-cooled He-air-CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-(CO) laser was operated in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-switched fashion yielding 20 CO laser lines below 5.0 μ. These laser lines were measured to occur from 4.7848 to 4.9880 μ. The lines were all identified to result from<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P(J)_{\upsilon,\upsilon'}</tex>CO vibrational-rotational transitions as low as<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon = 2:1</tex>. Nine such<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon = 2:1</tex>transitions were measured.

articleTitle: Resonant acoustooptic Q switching of high-gain lasers
A tunable CW dye laser
Theory of Fabry-Perot resonators with dielectric medium
abstract: A Fabry-Perot resonator filled with a dielectric slab is investigated using the Vainshtein method. Simple and explicit formulas are obtained for the diffraction loss, phase shift, and field distributions for both strip and circular mirrors. It is found that the presence of the dielectric reduces the diffraction loss, and causes mode confinement to certain degrees.

articleTitle: Single-wavelength CO2laser without dispersive elements
abstract: Observation of single-wavelength operation in a TEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</inf>mode laser at the 80-W level without the use of intracavity dispersive elements is reported. The output wavelength remains at the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P(20)</tex>line irrespective of cavity length changes, gas mixture, and excitation level for cavity lengths of about 4 m or longer.

articleTitle: New xenon laser line observed
abstract: A new xenon laser line was observed. Other parametric data are given.

articleTitle: Laser action in a flowing mixture of formic acid, nitrogen, and helium
abstract: Laser action has been observed in an electrically excited mixture of formic acid, nitrogen, and helium. The source of population inversion is shown to be CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>molecules that are formed by the dissociation of formic acid.

articleTitle: Cavity-loss dependence of erbium glass laser lines
abstract: The competition of the 1.536-μm and the 1.543-μm laser lines of erbium in zinc aluminophosphate glass is presented. Experimental results show that the 1.536-μm line oscillates under high-loss conditions whereas the 1.543-μm line oscillates under low-loss conditions. Both<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-switch and long-pulse data are included.

articleTitle: Flow lines on the poincaré sphere as an aid to the study of mode polarization in lasers
abstract: It is shown that the concept of flow lines on the Poincaré sphere is a useful tool in the study of mode polarization in lasers. As an example, a case from recent literature is analyzed.

articleTitle: Relative frequency stability of stable He-Ne gas laser structures
abstract: Enhanced He-Ne gas laser stability has been achieved by constructing the mirror and gas discharge tube as an integral unit. The primary components are made from Corning ULE and 99JJW ultralow thermal expansion materials; ultrahigh-vacuum-type materials are used throughout. The ambient pressure sensitivity of these 6328-Å laser structures is 2.5 MHz/torr. Preliminary beat frequency measurements between two lasers, under pressure and temperature-controlled conditions, have yielded a beat frequency spectral width of the order of 2 kHz over an interval of 1 s. This result was achieved without the use of any elaborate sound or vibration isolation. Improved isolation reduced the spectral width to 100 Hz for a measurement duration of 0.02 s. The single-structure mirror-discharge tube has provided relative output power stabilities of better than 3 parts in 1000 over a period of 12 h. The frequency-modulation sensitivity is 1.2 kHz/μA of discharge current, from dc to 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Amplification cross section of the 1.052-µ transition of Nd3+in POCl3- SnCl4-(H2O) system by three different methods
abstract: We report the measurement of the amplification cross section σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>of the Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>ion in the POCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-SnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-(H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O) system by three different methods. The first is based on the simultaneous measurement of the variation of fluorescence and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-spoiled laser emission. The second is purely spectroscopic. The third is based on the measurement of k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>at several temperatures. The two last methods give similar results. The most probable value is<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\sigma_{21} = 8.5 \times 10^{-20}</tex>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. An explanation for the lowest value<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\sim 6 \times 10^{-20}</tex>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>found with the first method is given.

articleTitle: Optical breakdown in gases of medium ionization potential
abstract: Breakdown threshold with ruby laser excitation has been determined for the gases Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, ICl, NO, NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Hg, and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, using argon as a reference. Our results indicate that threshold depends mainly on the ionization potential and that effects due to absorption in the visible region are secondary.

articleTitle: Iodine-atom laser emission in 2-2-2 trifluoroethyliodide
abstract: Lasing at 1.3 μ upon flash photolysis of 2-2-2 tri-fluoroethyliodide, CF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>I, has been observed on the<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P_{1/2}</tex>-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P_{3/2}</tex>magnetic dipole allowed transition of atomic iodine. Using an 800-J flash, a maximum peak power output of approximately 108 W for 10-μs duration at half-maximum intensity was obtained with a pressure of 17 torr CF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>I.

articleTitle: Active mode locking of a high-pressure pulsed N2O laser
abstract: Experimental results on the active mode locking of a transversely excited N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O laser at subatmospheric pressures are presented. Nanosecond pulses of 10.8-μ radiation were produced with typical peak-power outputs in the 100-kW range.

articleTitle: CW atomic oxygen laser at 4.56 µ
abstract: CW laser oscillation at 4.56 μ was observed in atomic oxygen produced in a magnetic induction discharge located at the upstream end of a fast flow system. The laser transition has been identified and an inversion scheme is proposed.

articleTitle: Mode-locked dual-polarization operation of a CO2laser
abstract: An electrooptic mode-locking technique for inducing simultaneous oscillation of spacially congruent, orthogonally polarized CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser modes is described. During mode-locked dual-polarization operation the frequency separation of the output components is determined by the magnitude of an intracavity birefringence. It can therefore be adjusted to any value consistent with the gain-profile width. The sensitivity of the technique is such that for intermode frequencies between 1 and 20 MHz, a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3 \times 10^{-4}</tex>radian intracavity phase modulation suffices to produce continuous, stable dual-polarization operation. Experimental results are given that indicate the dependence of the mode-locking phenomenon on modulator drive, intermode frequency, and laser cavity tuning. These results are compared with the prediction of simple theory.

articleTitle: CO2laser mode locking produced by sinusoidal cavity-length modulation
abstract: Mode locking of a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser through the use of cavity-length modulation is reported. A cavity end reflector was sinusoidally modulated along the cavity axis at a frequency equal to the quiescent axial mode interval. Phase-locked pulsing occurred at a rate equal to or twice the axial mode interval.

articleTitle: Picosecond structure in self-pulsing GaAs injection lasers
abstract: Partial mode locking has been observed in self-pulsing GaAs injection lasers using an optical correlation technique. The lasers are operated at room temperature and the self-pulsing occurs near the end of the injection current pulse. The pulsewidths are about 4 ps, which are the shortest observed in an injection laser.

articleTitle: Operation of a circularly polarized ring laser
abstract: Although there has been a large amount of experimental work published on the operation of the ring laser, nearly all of it was concerned with lasers operating in linearly polarized modes. In this paper the operation of a ring laser using the 1.153-μm wavelength transition of the He-Ne mixture in a cavity with no polarization constraint is reported. It was found that the two traveling waves operated in the same sense as circularly polarized modes and that there was no measurable coupling between the traveling waves via the amplifying medium, although there was still locking induced by coupling through cavity imperfections.

articleTitle: Single-longitudinal-mode Nd:YAG laser
Mobile laser Raman radar for monitoring stack effluent pollutants
Electrostrictive self-focusing of picosecond laser pulse trains
abstract: A nanosecond-long train of picosecond laser pulses theoretically can produce self-focusing by electrostriction, even though the trapping threshold for a single picosecond pulse is very high. The relative roles of electrostriction and various types of Kerr effect in picosecond pulse train self-focusing should be assessed.

articleTitle: Frequency modulation of a self-mode-locked dual-polarization CO2laser
abstract: Simultaneous active stabilization and frequency modulation of a mode-locked dual-polarization CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>laser is reported. Mode locking was maintained during frequency modulation through use of a self-regenerative feedback technique.

articleTitle: Time duration of output pulse in electron-beam-pumped CdS laser
abstract: Time duration of the output pulse of electron-beam-pumped CdS laser was investigated. It increased with increase of the excitation current density and was of the order of 100 ns at the beam voltage of 25 kV. It was shown experimentally that the quenching of the laser oscillation is due to the rise of the threshold current density as the result of the temperature rise in the active region of the crystal. The expression for the duration of laser oscillation based on this model was derived and compared with the experimental results. The dependence of the duration on the excitation current density was explained by this model.

articleTitle: Effect of competing laser transitions on intracavity optical second-harmonic generation
abstract: The effect on intracavity optical second-harmonic generation of additional laser transitions that compete for population inversion with the principal line is considered. It is shown that these transitions can limit the amount of harmonic generated unless some form of frequency-selective loss is provided. Parametric effects due to the presence of the second-harmonic radiation are also considered.

articleTitle: Optimum cut for a LiNbO3transverse light modulator
abstract: The most general expression for the half-wave voltage of a LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>transverse light modulator has been studied. As a result, a novel cut with a minimum half-wave voltage of 1440 V for amplitude modulation is proposed. A preliminary experimental verification confirms the promising theoretical results.

articleTitle: Random phase shifters for Fourier-transformed holograms
Velocity dependence of the gain of a CO2laser
abstract: Measurements of the small signal gain and saturation intensity of a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-He laser are made as a function of gas flow velocity over the range from<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\sim 0-10</tex>m/s. The small signal gain increases and the saturation intensity decreases with increased gas velocity. For intermediate flow velocities with a gas transit time in the laser of a second, the gain also depends on the direction of propagation of the amplified beam with respect to the gas flow. The directional dependence is due to an axial gradient in the saturation intensity. The transit time of the gas in the 2.5-m amplifier spans the time required for appreciable generation of CO by dissociation of the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>and the variation of the laser gain with velocity is attributed to the effects of CO on the inversion of the laser medium.

articleTitle: Large-area bistable ferroelectric ceramic polarization switches
Recent developments in dye lasers
Some recent advances and applications of optical parametric oscillators
Controllable phase-locked frequency splitting in two-frequency lasers
abstract: Lasers can be made to oscillate simultaneously at two frequencies by means of anisotropic or nonreciprocal resonator elements. A technique is described for stabilizing the resulting frequency separation by locking it to an external frequency source. The stabilized separation should be useful in optical heterodyne applications.

articleTitle: Short, efficient, and stable Nd:YAlG laser cavities using imaged mirrors
Simple linear-cavity TEM00-mode mode-locked ruby laser
Investigations and improvements of spectral and spatial resolution of a laser Doppler flowmeter
The F + H2O chemical laser
abstract: Laser oscillation, restricted by energy limitations to transitions from first vibrationallevel to ground state, has been observed from HF produced by the reaction of the F atom on H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O initiated by pulsed electric discharge in flowing mixed F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>0-He gases at 10 torr.

articleTitle: Polarization flip in the far-infrared HCN laser
abstract: The 90° polarization flip with hysteresis effect is observed at zero magnetic field in the CW 337-μm HCN laser. The flip disappears when the pressure is increased. In order to obtain the flip, it is necessary that under a constant pressure the input is larger than a threshold input at which the flip appears.

articleTitle: Digital light deflector with prisms and polarization switch based on the pockels effect with transverse field
Technology of continuous dye lasers
Hybrid optical data-processing system and its application to motion measurement and reconnaissance plotting
Air pollution detection and analysis using a wavelength tunable IR laser
New O II 6640-Å laser line
abstract: A prominent red laser line has been observed in oxygen and air at a wavelength of 6640.2 ± 1 Å. This line corresponds to the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3p^{2}S\min{1/2}\max{0}-3s^{2}P_{1/2}</tex>at 6640.90 Å of the O II spectrum. It is the strongest member of the observed emission lines close to the laser line.

articleTitle: Formation of self-trapped filaments by self focusing
abstract: It is shown that under suitable conditions the self-focusing of a Gaussian beam can lead to the self-trapped solution of Chiao et al. [2]. The properties of the focused region are described in detail.

articleTitle: Transverse excitation atmospheric pressure lasers
Flowing CO chemical laser experiments

abstract: Data giving the parametric dependence of plasma-induced fluctuations termed random noise and striation oscillations are presented for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>lasers and compared to He-Ne devices.

Phosphor system for converting far-infrared laser radiation to visible light
abstract: Criteria are given for the design of a directly visible phonon-assist phosphor device for converting far-infrared radiation to visible light. The operation of such a device, made with a readily available phosphor, is described. Two modes of conversion are demonstrated.

Image upconversion of infrared 10.6-µm radiation
